description: Both pieces of e_inf -- the edge energy and the run -- are explicit convergent series in q0, so the last unknown constant of the REV_n asymptotics no longer needs an enumeration to evaluate.  The run re-indexes to sum_d min(d,ell) T(d) - (ln q0/2) ell with T the second difference of eps along the progression, whose intercept resums to a single Lambert-type series; the edge's block-to-bulk tails resum the same way.  Both are checked against the direct pair sums and across a sweep of q, so they are identities rather than anchor coincidences.  What is NOT closed is the SEARCH: the maximising block [3,2,1,1,1] and run length 16 are inputs here, taken from PR #7335, and nothing in this probe proves them optimal.  Nor does anything here prove the limit e_k -> e_inf exists -- the upper bound on M_n is still open.

run_closed_form.formula: Xrun(ell) = sum_{d>=1} min(d,ell) T(d) - (ln q0 / 2) ell

checks.name: R1 the re-indexed run form reproduces the direct pair sum at every sampled length
checks.detail: 10 lengths from 1 to 32; worst difference 4.015e-56 against a floor of 1.0e-50 derived from the 55-digit truncation depths.  The direct side walks every straddling pair of the run; the closed side is one sum over distances, so this checks the re-indexing `sum_{j<=ell} sum_{d>=j} = sum_d min(d, ell)` rather than restating it

checks.name: R7 both halves of the run collect with the SAME multiplicity min(d, ell), separately
checks.detail: 8 lengths; worst difference 1.48e-58 against a floor of 1.0e-50.  R1 checks the SUM of the two halves, which a compensating error in the split would survive; this checks each half on its own, so it is the check that ties `EdgeDecoupling.sum_tails_eq_sum_min` (upward, condition `j < d`, kernel `eps(2d) - eps(2d+1)`) and `sum_heads_eq_sum_min` (downward, condition `ell <= j + d`, kernel `eps(2d) - eps(2d-1)`) to the two branches the probe actually walks.  The two halves are NOT equal to one another — they differ by up to 3.603, since the AP is asymmetric about a displaced row — so agreeing with the same multiplicity is a statement about the counting, not about a symmetry

checks.name: R2 the run's intercept agrees between the distance sum and the Lambert series
checks.detail: C = -0.65717794754589989394706076, difference 3.9e-55.  The two routes share no algebra: one sums the second difference `T(d)` over distances, the other expands `eps(m) = sum_r t^(-mr)/r` and resums, giving `C = -sum_r (1/r)(q^r - q^-r)^2 q^(-4r)/(1 - q^(-4r))^2`.  That second form is a single Lambert-type series in q0 with no reference to the lattice at all

checks.name: R3 the Lambert-tail edge form reproduces the direct pair sum on every sampled block
checks.detail: 8 blocks including the argmax [3, 2, 1, 1, 1]; worst difference 1.223e-58 against the 1.0e-50 floor.  Each block-to-bulk tail `sum_{d>=m}[eps(2d) - eps(2d+u)]` becomes `sum_r (1/r)(1 - q^(-2ur)) q^(-4mr)/(1 - q^(-4r))`, so the edge is a finite sum of Lambert series plus finitely many eps values — an explicit function of q, evaluated without any lattice sum

checks.name: R4 the closed forms reproduce #7335's searched e_inf
checks.detail: closed 2.439296455120784027065428843 against the searched 2.439296455120784027065428843 — difference -2.402e-30, at a floor of 2.44e-29 set by the 30 significant digits #7335's witness records.  #7335 obtained this number by exhaustive search over a shape class in scaled-integer arithmetic; this obtains it by evaluating two series.  Nothing is shared but the argmax shape

checks.name: R5 the run is asymptotically linear with slope -ln q0 / 2 to the predicted residual, and the asymptote is NOT reached at the length e_inf uses
checks.detail: the secant slope over ell = 100..200 is -0.0521703601597597561598 against -ln q0/2 = -0.05217036015975975615795, differing by -1.851e-21 against a computed bound of 6.316e-20 — the largest per-step residual `sum_{d>100} T(d)` in that window.  So the linear part is the quadratic cost and nothing else, and the approach is at exactly the rate T predicts.  At ell = 16, the length e_inf actually uses, the exact form and the asymptote still differ by 0.0003114, four orders above anything else in this arc, falling to 9.827e-19 by ell = 96.  So `min(d, ell)` is load-bearing and the intercept C is a limit rather than a shortcut — quoting `C - (ln q0/2) ell` as Xrun would corrupt e_inf in its fourth decimal

checks.name: R6 both closed forms hold across a sweep of q — identities, not anchor coincidences
checks.detail: six values of q from 1.03 to 2.5, spanning the substrate anchor; worst difference across all three identities 1.695e-54 against the 1.0e-50 floor.  This is the check that separates an identity from a numerical coincidence: a closed form fitted to one anchor would not survive q = 2.5, where eps decays an order faster and the series depths derived above shrink accordingly

verdict: e_inf = 2 * E_edge + Xrun(2s) is an explicit convergent series in q0 once its argmax shape is fixed: the run re-indexes to a distance sum whose intercept is a Lambert series, and the edge's tails resum the same way.  Verified against the direct pair sums, against PR #7335's independently searched value to the 30 digits its witness records, and across a sweep of q -- identities, not anchor coincidences.  The SEARCH for the argmax shape is not closed, and the existence of the limit is still open.
